name: Jamie Haller
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $462 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Women's loafers, flats and boots around $600, plus ready-to-wear tailoring, denim, knits, bags and belts, sold through its Montecito store, website and named stockists.

quote.q: I am not a shoe designer who started making clothes. For me, designing clothing is like a coming home to who I have always been.

opview: “I am not a shoe designer who started making clothes. For me, designing clothing is like a coming home to who I have always been.” — Jamie Haller, founder, Homepage, shop-jamiehaller.com

facts_read.source: brand site (home, about, stockists, season pages, terms); Vinted catalogue + item page; TRR designer index; B Lab directory; GOTS database

price_read.sublines: Jamie Haller womenswear and shoes; EXCLUDED: men's loafers, handbags, accessories, insurance

doors.note: Domain differs: jamiehaller.com is the founder's interior-design site; product is footwear (loafers) and apparel at shop-jamiehaller.com. One own shop (The Post Montecito, Santa Barbara). Stockist page lists ~80 US wholesale stockists (incl. Nordstrom, Jeffrey) — not rowed.

fibre.sample: all 67 styles read (154 'Womenswear' feed records collapsed on the title before ' in <colour>'); shoes, bags and accessories out of scope; 6 styles without a fe

craft_evidence.owned: no — makers described but not named or owned: 'a B corp certified denim factory and laundry' in Los Angeles, 'a generational family factory' in Italy, 'a boutique designer knitting factory' in Hong Ko
craft_evidence.makers: no — described by type and place, never by name
craft_evidence.mills: no — cloth origin given ('Japanese cotton poplin', 'Italian stretch denim', 'Italian lamb'), no mill named
craft_evidence.madein: ~25% (about 17 of 67 styles state where they are made or tailored: USA / Los Angeles, Italy, Hong Kong)
craft_evidence.heritage: dated — collection launched 2020 by a '22 year veteran in the Los Angeles fashion landscape'
craft_evidence.process: partial — denim laundering and finishing described per style (whiskers, sanding, fading; raw rinse); no process page
craft_evidence.reasoning: About a quarter of product pages say where the piece is made and describe the kind of factory (an LA B-corp denim factory, a family leather factory in Italy, a Hong Kong knitter), and cloth origins are given, but no maker or mill is named. That is more than a country label but short of the named makers a 3 needs.
